cleanIntro: Walther's PP/PPK book is the manual for this pistol's mechanism, and it is a short one because the gun is simple: the PPK/S comes apart into three pieces with no tools and no loose small parts. What the book never prints is the designation PPK/S - it covers the PP and the PPK, and the PPK/S is the PPK's slide and barrel on the PP's frame. Every control in the procedure below is on your gun. One thing the book cannot tell you is your magazine capacity, because it tabulates the PP and the PPK separately and yours takes the longer frame's magazine; count your own.

steps.title: Safety catch ON before anything - loading, unloading or stripping
steps.action: Apply the safety catch first. Walther's rule for this pistol is that it is loaded, unloaded and dismantled with the safety applied, and with the muzzle pointed at the ground throughout.
steps.prose: On a PP-series pistol the safety catch is a decocker as well: pushing it down drops the hammer while blocking the striker, so 'safety on' is also 'hammer down' and it is the correct state for everything that follows. Muzzle at the ground is not decoration either - it is the direction that keeps a chambered round pointed somewhere survivable.
steps.quote: Ensure that the pistol is being either loaded or unloaded or dismantled while the safety catch is applied. Whenever doing so, point the muzzle towards the ground.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistolen Mod. PP/PPK
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Instrucciones de uso — PP/PPK Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/ES), 13pp — Advice on the use of the WALTHER pistols model PP/PPK, printed p.8 (OCR page 5)

steps.title: Magazine out with the thumb button
steps.action: With the safety catch applied, press the magazine release button with the thumb and withdraw the magazine.
steps.prose: The button sits on the left of the frame behind the trigger. On a PPK/S the magazine is the longer PP-frame one with a finger extension or a flat floorplate depending on how yours was sold - so do not judge whether it is empty by its length. Look at the witness holes if it has them, and count.
steps.quote: Apply the safety catch. Press the magazine release button with the thumb and withdraw the magazine.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistolen Mod. PP/PPK
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Instrucciones de uso — PP/PPK Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/ES), 13pp — To remove the magazine, printed p.9 (OCR page 5)

steps.title: Slide fully back, then check the barrel is clear with your eyes
steps.action: Remove the magazine and pull the slide fully back. Any cartridge in the barrel is extracted and ejected. Then check carefully that the barrel is free.
steps.prose: Magazine first and then the slide, in that order, or you simply chamber another round. Pull it all the way to the stop rather than partway - a short stroke on a blowback pistol can extract without ejecting and leave the case loose in the action. Then look, with light, down through the ejection port.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine and pull the slide fully back. Cartridge in the barrel will be extracted and ejected. Check carefully that barrel is free.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistolen Mod. PP/PPK
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Instrucciones de uso — PP/PPK Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/ES), 13pp — Unloading, printed p.16 (OCR page 9)

steps.title: The book cannot tell you your capacity - count it yourself
steps.action: Do not take a round count from the technical data. Walther tabulates the Mod. PP and the Mod. PPK separately, and a PPK/S is the PPK's slide on the PP's frame - so it takes the longer frame's magazine, not the one the PPK column describes.
steps.prose: This is the one place where reading this book as though it were written for your exact designation would mislead you, and it is worth naming plainly rather than papering over. Load your own magazine to capacity once, on the bench, with dummy rounds or by counting live rounds in and out, and know the number.
steps.quote: The pistol can be dismantled in a matter without using any tools in the main parts. There are no loose parts.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistolen Mod. PP/PPK
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Instrucciones de uso — PP/PPK Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/ES), 13pp — Advice on the use of the WALTHER pistols model PP/PPK, printed p.8 (OCR page 5)

steps.title: Trigger guard down and sideways, resting on the frame
steps.action: With the safety catch applied and the magazine out, and the chamber confirmed empty, pull the trigger guard downward, push it sideways with the index finger, and let it rest on the underside of the frame. Hold it there with your index finger. Then pull the slide fully back, lift it off at the rear and let it glide forward.
steps.prose: The trigger guard IS the takedown latch on this design - there is no takedown lever, no slide stop to pull. Pull it straight down first and only then push it sideways; twisting it while it is still seated is how they get bent. It must stay held over to one side for the whole of the slide's travel, so use the finger you are not lifting with.
steps.quote: Apply the safety catch and remove the magazine. Make sure that the chamber is empty. Pull the trigger guard downward, push it sideways with the index finger, and allow it to rest on the underside of the frame. Hold the trigger guard in this position with the index finger. Pull the slide fully back, then lift if off and allow to glide forward.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistolen Mod. PP/PPK
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Instrucciones de uso — PP/PPK Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/ES), 13pp — To dismantle the pistol, printed p.16 (OCR page 9)
steps.warn: Never allow the hammer to drop freely forward while the pistol is thus partly dismantled.

steps.title: Never let the hammer fall with the slide off
steps.action: With the slide off, do not let the hammer snap forward. Keep the safety applied and keep your fingers out of the hammer's path while the frame is bare.
steps.prose: There is nothing for the hammer to strike once the slide is gone, so it slams into the frame instead. Repeat that a few times and you peen the hammer nose and the frame face - a wear pattern that shows up years later as light strikes. Walther prints the warning in bold for a reason.
steps.quote: Never allow the hammer to drop freely forward while the pistol is thus partly dismantled.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistolen Mod. PP/PPK
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Instrucciones de uso — PP/PPK Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/ES), 13pp — To dismantle the pistol, printed p.16 (OCR page 9)

steps.title: Field strip complete - three main components, and that is the limit
steps.action: Frame, slide and barrel with its recoil spring. Walther states the pistol has been taken down into its three main components for cleaning and that any further dismantling should be carried out only by a skilled craftsman.
steps.prose: On a PPK/S the barrel is fixed to the frame and the recoil spring lives around it, so 'three components' really means the slide comes off and everything else stays where it is. That is the whole strip and it is enough - the bore, the breech face, the feed ramp, the spring and the rails are all in front of you.
steps.quote: The pistol has been taken down into its three main components for cleaning. Any further dismantling should be carried out only by a skilled craftsman.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistolen Mod. PP/PPK
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Instrucciones de uso — PP/PPK Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/ES), 13pp — Cleaning, printed p.19 (OCR page 10)

deepAbsentReason: Walther publishes nothing deeper for the PP/PPK than the three-component strip. The cleaning page states the pistol has been taken down into its three main components for cleaning and then says any further dismantling should be carried out only by a skilled craftsman. There is no slide-internals procedure, no firing-pin removal and no frame disassembly anywhere in the book. ⛔ PROHIBITED IS PER-PROCEDURE, NOT PER-FAMILY: what Walther bars is further dismantling, and the full routine clean it does publish is walked above. The forbidden operation is carried in this spec's `prohibits` field. Nothing was invented to fill the gap.

cleaning.name: BARREL, CHAMBER & FEED RAMP
tasks: Brush the bore from the chamber end where you can and follow with patches until they come out clean
Clean the chamber itself - a blowback .380 headspaces on the case mouth and a dirty chamber is what makes cases stick
Wipe the feed ramp; a PPK/S feeds at a steep angle and a fouled ramp is the usual cause of a nose-up stoppage
Check the bore against a light before the pistol is put away

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BREECH FACE & RECOIL SPRING
tasks: Clean the breech face and around the extractor claw without levering the extractor out
Wipe the inside of the slide and its rail cuts, then dry them before oiling
Wipe the recoil spring and the barrel it sits on - note which end of the spring is the narrow one before you move it
Keep solvent away from the grip panels and out of the frame's lockwork

cleaning.name: OIL & STORAGE
tasks: A thin film of good quality oil on the metal, and the excess wiped off - this is a small pistol with tight clearances
A drop on the rails and on the barrel where the slide bears; nothing inside the frame
Walther recommends storing the pistol uncocked and unsecured rather than cocked
Do not store it in leather or anything else that holds moisture against the finish

reassembly: Push the recoil spring back onto the barrel with the narrower end first - Walther states that explicitly and it is the one way it can go wrong invisibly.
Bring the slide onto the barrel from the front, push it fully to the rear and let the rear of the slide drop onto the frame rails.
Let the slide run forward under its own spring, then release the trigger guard and press it back up until it snaps into place.
Check the trigger guard is fully seated and flush before the pistol is handled as a firearm again.
fncheck: With the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty: the trigger guard must be fully back up and flush; the slide should run its full stroke and return to battery under its own spring; the safety catch should move down with a positive detent and drop the hammer without the hammer touching the striker; the double-action pull should cock and release the hammer smoothly and the single-action notch should hold at full cock without following; and the magazine should drop free when the button is pressed. Walther's standing advice for this pistol is to store it uncocked.
